outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Enterprise and AI software, led by Palantir, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Adobe
strongest.reason: all rallied sharply as the broader 'AI isn't eating software' thesis gained traction, with fresh alliance news (Palantir-PwC), earnings momentum (Salesforce), and positive analyst revisions ahead of upcoming reports (Adobe) all contributing

strongest.area: AI infrastructure dealmaking, led by Nvidia and Microsoft
strongest.reason: Nvidia's confirmed $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition and Microsoft's new Azure-revenue disclosure plan both reinforced investor confidence in the durability of AI infrastructure spending

weakest.area: Chip-design software and select chip-equipment names, including Cadence and Teradyne
weakest.reason: both pulled back after strong recent runs, with Teradyne hit by a valuation-driven analyst downgrade and Cadence giving back gains with no clear company-specific catalyst, as semiconductor-tariff headlines added sector-wide uncertainty

weakest.area: Middle East-driven macro pressure on oil and safe-haven assets
weakest.reason: Iran's strikes on Gulf-ally Kuwait kept WTI near $92 and gold above $4,490, even as hopes that the escalation proves short-lived helped stocks and crypto recover some poise

outlook.nextStep: Zscaler's fiscal Q4 report after today's close and any concrete follow-through from Tesla's Cybercab event are the most immediate, trackable catalysts worth watching before drawing conclusions. The semiconductor-tariff headlines and the still-fluid Iran situation are slower-moving, higher-uncertainty risks probably better monitored over the next several sessions than acted on from a single day's headlines.

signals.title: Iran strikes Gulf ally Kuwait as Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate further
signals.body: Iran extended its military actions to strike Kuwait, sending WTI crude toward $92 and Brent above $96 a barrel. Trump's comments that the exchange would be short-lived helped cap the rally, and markets broadly interpreted the situation as a serious but potentially containable escalation.
signals.focus: a genuine tail risk worth watching closely for further headlines rather than a reason to act on either side yet

signals.title: Fed rate-hike odds cool from this week's highs
signals.body: Market-implied odds of a 25-basis-point September hike eased to roughly the mid-50s to 60s percent range from near 70% earlier in the week, even with energy-driven inflation risk still elevated from the Iran conflict. The pullback in odds helped the 10-year yield ease slightly and gave stocks room to rebound.
signals.focus: probably better watched than acted on until the September 16 FOMC meeting provides more clarity

signals.title: Nvidia confirms $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face
signals.body: After weeks of speculation, Nvidia confirmed it will acquire the open-source AI model platform Hugging Face for roughly $12.9 billion, its largest AI acquisition to date. The deal is framed as expanding Nvidia's reach across the open-model AI stack even as some of its largest customers develop their own custom chips.
signals.focus: worth a closer look as a signal of where Nvidia sees its next growth vector, beyond just near-term price action

signals.title: Enterprise software rally broadens beyond Salesforce
signals.body: Palantir, ServiceNow, and Adobe all posted big gains alongside continued strength in Salesforce, as investor concerns that AI would cannibalize subscription software revenue keep easing. Palantir's rebound followed an expanded PwC alliance a day after its worst session in seven months.
signals.focus: worth watching whether this breadth holds or proves to be a short covering-driven bounce, especially for the more richly-valued names

signals.title: Tesla's Cybercab launch event is today's key robotics catalyst
signals.body: Tesla shares jumped ahead of an invite-only Cybercab event in Austin, Texas, with company teasers promising a design with no steering wheel or pedals. Investors are looking for concrete updates on production timelines and the broader Optimus and robotaxi rollout.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the binary, event-driven nature of today's catalyst

signals.title: Fresh U.S. semiconductor tariffs reportedly on the way
signals.body: Commerce Secretary Lutnick said semiconductor tariffs are coming, reviving trade-policy uncertainty for chipmakers including Nvidia, AMD, Taiwan Semiconductor, and memory names like Micron. Reports suggest the tariffs could extend to a broader range of tech products built alongside chips.
signals.focus: a policy risk probably worth tracking for details rather than trading on the initial headline

signals.title: Zscaler reports fiscal Q4 earnings after today's close
signals.body: Zscaler's print caps a strong week for cybersecurity earnings after both CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks posted upbeat results, with CrowdStrike separately using its Fal.Con conference to launch several new AI-security products and draw a string of price-target increases.
signals.focus: worth watching closely after today's close rather than positioning ahead of the print
